sentences.text: Daniel Okafor, a solicitor in the employment team, attended the meeting with Aisha Rahman, the client, and Sophie Grant, the trainee (Ln 5, Ln 6).
The purpose of the meeting was for Daniel Okafor to get the client's story and dates straight, and then to advise on what happens next (Ln 8).
Aisha Rahman worked for Northgate Logistics Limited, which is described as the big warehouse off the ring road by the retail park with blue cladding (Ln 11).
She started working there on the fifth of March twenty eighteen (Ln 14), initially as a picker on the floor for general picking (Ln 16).
She was promoted to team leader of inbound goods in June twenty twenty-one (Ln 16, Ln 18).
Her hours were full time, four on four off days, from seven till seven quarter past with handover (Ln 20).
Her basic pay was twenty-nine thousand four hundred a year, with a shift allowance of about eighteen hundred a year (Ln 23, Ln 25).
Aisha Rahman has type one diabetes, which she has had since she was fourteen (Ln 31).
She informed her manager, Linda Chu, about her diabetes when she started (Ln 38).
The arrangement with Linda Chu was that if she needed to step off for five minutes, she could tell a colleague to cover, and Linda never had an issue with this (Ln 42).
Linda Chu left at the end of last year and was replaced by Gary Whitlock, who started on the twelfth of January (Ln 56, Ln 57).
Gary Whitlock sent an email on the second of February stating that everyone must take breaks at fixed times, and no one could leave the dock outside those times without his say-so (Ln 62).
Aisha Rahman has written some things down on her phone (Ln 9).
She has the original contract from twenty eighteen (Ln 29).
She has a certificate from when she was team leader in twenty twenty-three (Ln 52).
She has the occupational health report, which was dated the twenty-second of April (Ln 73).
She believes the OH report was sent to her personal email by HR (Ln 76).
She has the invite letter to the disciplinary meeting and the dismissal letter, dated the fourteenth of August (Ln 124, Ln 145).
She has the payslips for May, June, July, and the final August one (Ln 188).
Marcus Bell, a first aider, took a photo of her phone showing her sensor reading on the ninth of July (Ln 99, Ln 101).
She has a copy of her appeal email (Ln 192).
She has a spreadsheet tracking her job applications (Ln 224).
Aisha Rahman's primary objective is for the employer to admit they were wrong (Ln 234).
Her second objective is to receive a proper reference so she can get a job (Ln 234).
Compensation is considered secondary to the first two objectives (Ln 235).
She also wishes for the employer to sort out the break thing for other employees who have conditions like epilepsy (Ln 236).
Daniel Okafor advised that she should not sign anything without talking to the solicitor first, even if it appears to be a formality (Ln 176).
The solicitor advised that in employment tribunal claims, the time limits are very short and strict (Ln 251).
The solicitor advised that she must notify ACAS within three months less one day of the dismissal, meaning the last day to contact ACAS is the thirteenth of November twenty twenty-six (Ln 254).
The solicitor stated that the clock for the claim runs from the effective date of termination, which is the fourteenth of August (Ln 264).
The solicitor advised that type one diabetes is very likely to count as a disability under the Equality Act (Ln 273).
The solicitor identified potential claims as unfair dismissal, discrimination arising from disability, and failure to make reasonable adjustments (Ln 274).

The solicitor noted procedural concerns, including Gary chairing the disciplinary hearing when it was his complaint, the lack of previous warnings, not being given the notes, and the letter not mentioning the diabetes (Ln 275).
The solicitor stated that he would give a range of figures for compensation once he has the payslips and job search information (Ln 283).
The solicitor advised that a reference can often be negotiated as part of a settlement through ACAS (Ln 284).
The solicitor advised that she should ask Marcus whether he would be willing to give a statement, but not to approach Tomasz yet (Ln 305).
Aisha Rahman must email the OH report, Marcus's photo of the sensor, and any outstanding payslips by this Friday, the twenty-fifth (Ln 289).
Aisha Rahman must check with Castleford Mutual regarding legal expenses cover by Monday, the twenty-eighth, and send the policy schedule and wording (Ln 291).
Aisha Rahman must write a timeline of everything discussed in her own words by next Friday, the second of October (Ln 293).
Sophie Grant will draft the subject access request to Northgate by Monday, and Daniel Okafor will check it before it goes out on Tuesday (Ln 297).
Daniel Okafor will send a letter confirming today's advice and funding options by Tuesday the twenty-ninth (Ln 304).
Daniel Okafor and Aisha Rahman are scheduled to meet again on Thursday the eighth of October at ten o'clock (Ln 309).
